crie.title: Azure Analyze via signed URL — execution-data isolation boundary
crie.purpose: Mint a short-lived storage signed URL, hand it to Azure Document Intelligence, and return ONLY the Azure submit response. The signed URL never leaves this workflow and is never persisted anywhere.
crie.roadmap: Object Storage PR-3. Exists solely to satisfy a platform constraint; it holds no business logic.
crie.why_a_separate_workflow: Measured on n8n 2.29.9: a runtime-minted URL emitted in ANY node's output is written to the executions table (Probe G). saveDataSuccessExecution / saveDataErrorExecution are PER-WORKFLOW settings, so isolating the mint+submit in a child set to 'none' is the only supported way to keep the URL out of execution data while BOTH credentials stay in the n8n credential store. A Code node cannot do it instead: helpers.httpRequestWithAuthentication is explicitly unsupported there ('The function "helpers.httpRequestWithAuthentication" is not supported in the Code Node'), so a single-node mint+consume would force both secrets into $env.

isolation_contract.settings: saveDataSuccessExecution=none, saveDataErrorExecution=none, saveExecutionProgress=false. This workflow persists NOTHING.
isolation_contract.returns: Only { statusCode, headers } — the Azure submit response shape. Never the signed URL, never the storage response, never Azure request metadata containing the URL.
isolation_contract.errors: Every node that can see the URL swallows its own errors (onError + neverError). Failures are re-raised as REDACTED errors. A raw error would propagate into the PARENT's error record — measured: 1 occurrence when raw, 0 when redacted.
isolation_contract.measured: Isolation verified during the PR-3 investigation: success path 0 sentinel occurrences, redacted-failure path 0, raw-failure path 1 (the case this design forbids). Child execution records created: 0 in all runs.

crie.return_shape_rationale: Returns the Azure fullResponse shape { statusCode, headers } deliberately, so SW-005's existing 'submit() — capture pollUrl' adapter consumes it UNCHANGED. The poll loop, retry budget, terminal-failure handling and HUMAN_REVIEW routing therefore all keep working exactly as before.
crie.failure_routing: An Azure response of ANY status is returned as data, preserving today's routing (non-202 -> terminal submit failure -> OCR failed -> HUMAN_REVIEW). Only a mint failure — a failure mode that does not exist today — raises a redacted workflow error.
crie.credentials_on_import: BIND BEFORE USE. 'Mint Signed URL' needs the Supabase storage credential (generic header auth, not yet created). 'Submit to Azure' uses the existing 'Azure Document Intelligence' credential, unchanged.
crie.input: { storageKey, azureEndpoint, azureModel, signedUrlTtlSeconds, correlationId }. Bucket and storage endpoint come from $env (non-secret config, same split as SW-029). NO SECRET IS READ FROM $env.

nodes.name: When Called by SW-005
nodes.notes: inputSource:'passthrough' (LOWERCASE t) per the frozen SW I/O contract. Receives JSON only — no binary crosses this boundary on the signed-URL path.

nodes.name: Mint Signed URL
nodes.notes: Mints a short-lived signed URL. onError + neverError so a storage failure becomes DATA rather than a raw error — a raw error here would carry the request URL into the parent's error record. The credential holds the secret; $env carries only non-secret endpoint/bucket.

nodes.name: Build urlSource
nodes.notes: The only place the absolute signed URL is constructed. Its output stays inside this workflow. On mint failure it raises a redacted error naming the storage KEY (not sensitive) and never the URL.

nodes.name: Submit to Azure
nodes.notes: Azure fetches the document itself from the signed URL — the bytes never enter n8n. Uses the EXISTING Azure credential, unchanged. onError + neverError so an Azure error becomes data: the request body contains the signed URL, so a raw error here would leak it.

nodes.name: Return Submit Response
nodes.notes: The whitelist is deliberate: only statusCode and headers are returned. Anything added here must be re-checked against the isolation contract.
